issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may permit a party to amend its pleadings to raise a new plea even when the material needed to decide that plea is not already before the court.
material_facts: The Government sought to amend its written statement during the appeal to plead res judicata based on a separate suit.
The Government explained that it had not sought amendment earlier because an appeal in the separate suit was pending, and it sought amendment soon after that decision was affirmed.
The High Court accepted the explanation and permitted the amendment.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court acted within its discretion in permitting the amendment, and there was no ground to interfere with that decision.
issues.legal_principle: There is no bar against an appellate court permitting an amendment to pleadings to raise a new plea. The court applies the usual principles governing amendments, including considering delay and the reason for seeking amendment at the appellate stage. The fact that material needed to decide the plea is not already before the court is relevant but is not, by itself, a prohibition against amendment.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and amendment_sought_to_raise_new_plea and delay_reasonably_explained and application_made_promptly

predicates.appeal_proceeding: The matter is being considered by a court hearing an appeal.
predicates.amendment_sought_to_raise_new_plea: A party asks to amend its pleadings in order to raise a plea not previously pleaded.
predicates.delay_reasonably_explained: The party gives a reason accepted by the court for not seeking the amendment earlier.
predicates.application_made_promptly: The party seeks the amendment soon after the circumstance explaining the earlier delay ends.

issues.definition: When a party seeks a new plea by amendment during an appeal, explains the delay and applies promptly, the amendment may be permitted.

issues.legal_issue: A later suit is barred by res judicata when the same issue between the same parties has already been finally decided, even if the suits have different subject matters, additional parties, or different material is placed before the later court.
material_facts: A prior damages suit and the later suit for a declaration involved the same plaintiff and the State as the contesting defendant on the issue of whether the agreement and surety bond were unenforceable for non-compliance with Article 299 of the Constitution.
The prior court rejected that challenge, finding that the agreement had been ratified and acted upon, and its decision was affirmed on appeal.
The later suit included additional parties and did not expressly plead ratification, and the subject matter of the suits differed.
The prior decision was final, and the additional parties and differences between the suits did not alter the identity of the issue between the plaintiff and the State.
issues.conclusion: The plea of res judicata was properly upheld because the issue in the later suit had already been decided between the same parties in the prior suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, res judicata may apply where the issue in the later suit is the same as an issue previously decided between the same parties, or parties under whom they claim, by a competent court and the other statutory conditions are met. It is not necessary for every party or the overall subject matter of the suits to be identical. Once the issue and parties are the same, the fact that material supporting the earlier decision is not placed before the later court does not prevent the bar from applying.

rule.if: successive_suits and same_parties_on_issue and issue_identical and prior_decision_final and prior_court_competent

predicates.successive_suits: A party raises an issue in a later suit after that issue arose in an earlier suit.
predicates.same_parties_on_issue: The parties contesting the issue in the later suit are the same as those who contested it in the earlier suit, or claim under them.
predicates.issue_identical: The issue in the later suit is the same issue that was determined in the earlier suit.
predicates.prior_decision_final: The earlier court's determination of the issue became final.
predicates.prior_court_competent: The earlier issue was decided by a court competent to determine it.

issues.definition: When successive suits involve the same parties on an identical issue that was finally decided by a competent court, the later issue is barred.

issues.legal_issue: A party may be refused permission to raise on appeal a plea that was not pursued before the intermediate appellate court.
material_facts: The plaintiff had challenged the rejection of the surety-discharge plea by filing cross-objections in the High Court.
No argument was advanced in support of those cross-objections, and the High Court dismissed them.
The plaintiff sought to raise the surety-discharge plea again in the further appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to permit the plaintiff to raise the surety-discharge plea again because it had not been pursued before the High Court and there was no justification for reopening it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its discretion to refuse consideration of a plea that was not pursued before the intermediate appellate court; it identified no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this ruling.

predicates.further_appeal_proceeding: The matter is before a further appellate court.
predicates.issue_not_pursued_in_intermediate_appeal: The party did not advance argument on the issue before the intermediate appellate court.

issues.definition: In a further appeal, an issue not pursued before the intermediate appellate court may be left unconsidered.
